title: OTLP ingress policy engine: circuit-breaker + SLO-aware sparse export
creator: Lina Chen
description: Build an OTLP ingress policy engine that runs at the trace gateway to protect downstream tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, vendor endpoints) by applying circuit-breakers, adaptive throttles, and SLO-aware sparse-export rules. The engine should allow per-tenant and per-backend policies, emit observability for decisions, and preserve important span continuity metadata when sparsifying exports.
background: We observed multiple incidents where noisy tenants or high-cardinality services caused sustained overload on third-party Tempo clusters and vendor collectors. Existing global batching + retry logic reacts too late and wastes credits. We need a lightweight policy layer at the OTLP ingress to proactively decide when to slow down or sparsify exports for a given tenant/backend, and to surface those decisions in dashboards and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress policy engine accepts policy config per tenant and per backend (JSON/YAML).
Engine exposes circuit-breaker states and adaptive throttle metrics via Prometheus (per-tenant, per-backend).
Supports two sparsification modes: probabilistic span drop and prefix-based keep rules that preserve root/critical spans.
Span continuity preserved: when a span is dropped, an annotated light-span (sparse-marker) is emitted so downstream traces can be correlated for sampling analysis.
Fail-open/fail-closed selectable per policy; default is fail-open for non-critical tenants.
E2E tests (unit + integration) covering policy enforcement, metrics emission, and compatibility with Tempo/Jaeger exporters.
implementation_notes: Prototype will be placed as a light filter in the existing otlp-ingest service. Key components: policy evaluator (in Rust), local token-bucket adaptors per backend, circuit-breaker state machine (with exponential backoff and health probes), and sparse-export transformer that replaces full span payloads with compact markers when configured.
tradeoffs_decisions: Decision: Perform policy evaluation inline in the ingest path to minimize decision latency (adds ~1.5ms median). Alternative was async sidecar; rejected because it increases loss window.
Trade-off: Probabilistic sparsification risks losing tail span detail. Mitigation: prefix-based keep rules and emitting sparse-markers to allow downstream correlation and sampling reconstruction.
Decision: Default to fail-open for trial tenants to avoid accidental telemetry loss; enterprise tenants can opt-in to strict failure behavior.
Trade-off: Per-tenant policies increase config complexity. We'll provide sane defaults and a UI in Console later (follow-up PM ticket).
dashboards_and_alerts: Grafana: OTLP Ingest / Policy Decisions (per-tenant circuit state)
SLO: Percent of spans dropped by policy > 5% for critical tenants -> pager
Alert: exporter-backend-retry-rate spike -> create incident runbook link
progress_updates: 2026-01-26: Spike completed to measure inline latency impact (proto evaluator in Go). Median added latency ~1.5ms, p99 ~12ms for large payloads.
2026-01-30: Rust policy evaluator prototype started; initial CI test harness for policy configs checked in.
2026-02-04: Design review with Observability and Platform; agreed on sparse-marker schema and Prometheus metric names.
2026-02-10: Integration tests added for Tempo + Jaeger exporters; discovered Jaeger batch format rejects zero-length spans — implemented compact-marker workaround.
risks: Misconfigured sparsification could hide customer-impacting errors; mitigated by conservative defaults and audit logs.
Additional inline latency may affect low-latency customers; we will gate heavy rules behind per-tenant flags and measure with canary traffic.
Compatibility edge-cases per backend (some vendors reject lightweight markers) — will maintain per-backend translation layers.
comments: PM (Sofia Rivera): Please ensure we expose a simple metric for "percent_spans_sparsified" keyed by tenant so product can create automated notifications.
Infra (Hiro Tanaka): For enterprise Private deployments we need a toggle to disable outbound marker emission for air-gapped collectors.
Security (Anika Bose): Confirm sparse-markers do not contain any PII; add a policy test for redaction.
